title: Animal Lifespans: How Long Animals Live
intro: How long an animal lives depends on its size, its metabolism, its environment and how many things are trying to eat it. As a rule, bigger animals live longer, cold-blooded animals outlive warm-blooded animals of the same size, and animals in human care outlive their wild relatives because they are protected from predators, hunger and disease. The table gives the typical lifespan in the wild for every animal in the database, with the lifespan in human care where it is known.

title: Animal Weights: How Much Animals Weigh
intro: Animal weights span more than eleven orders of magnitude, from insects weighing a few milligrams to the blue whale at well over 100 tonnes. The figures here are typical adult ranges. In many species males and females differ substantially, and the note on each animal page explains which sex is heavier.

title: Animal Sizes: Height and Length
intro: Size is measured differently for different body plans. Four-legged mammals are measured to the shoulder, upright animals such as giraffes, ostriches and penguins by standing height, and whales, fish, snakes and lizards by total length. Some birds and insects are best described by wingspan. Each row says which measurement is used.

title: Animal Speeds: How Fast Animals Run, Swim and Fly
intro: Top speeds are among the least reliable animal statistics, because they are rarely measured under controlled conditions and the most quotable number tends to get repeated. The figures here are maximum burst speeds from the better-supported end of the range, with a note on how each is achieved: running, swimming, level flight or a dive.

title: Animal Gestation and Incubation Periods
intro: Gestation is the time between conception and birth in animals that bear live young. For egg-laying animals the equivalent figure is the incubation or egg development period, from laying to hatching. In mammals, gestation rises with body size, from about three weeks in mice to nearly two years in elephants; marsupials are the exception, with very short pregnancies followed by a long period in the pouch.

title: Animal Diets: What Animals Eat
intro: Animals are grouped by what they mainly eat. Carnivores eat other animals, herbivores eat plants, and omnivores eat both. More specific labels describe specialists: insectivores, fish-eating piscivores, nectar feeders, filter feeders that strain plankton from the water, and detritivores that recycle dead material. Few animals are strict about it; many herbivores take the occasional egg or insect.

title: Animal Conservation Status (IUCN Red List)
intro: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species sorts species by extinction risk into Least Concern, Near Threatened, Vulnerable, Endangered, Critically Endangered, Extinct in the Wild and Extinct, with Data Deficient for species too poorly known to assess. Domestic animals are not assessed, and many invertebrates have never been evaluated. Assessments are revised as new data arrive, so treat the status here as a guide and follow the Red List link on each page for the current listing.
